fields.description:
## Summary

The FIRST `initialize` handled by a freshly deployed mcp container was reported to take far longer
than the 30-second default startup timeout most MCP clients use, while every later client sees a
warm process and connects instantly.

## Investigation outcome (see the RCA comment for the full measurement table)

Measured on current `origin/main` against the live box across three real deploys:

- A cold authenticated `initialize`, fired at the exact cutover instant against a 5.5-second-old
  container and the real 2.2 GB store, completes in **0.030 s**. The reported 8.43 s does not
  reproduce on current `main`.
- The in-process first-`/mcp`-request warm-up is **7 ms** (8.9 ms vs 1.8 ms), importing two
  trivial modules. Store size, boto3/bedrock, auth, and background provisioning were each
  measured and **refuted** as contributors to handshake latency.
- The only multi-second cost is **5.5-7.5 s of Python process startup before uvicorn binds**,
  during which the published host port is already bound by docker-proxy, so an arriving
  connection is accepted and then hangs rather than being refused.
- **`/health` returning 200 is not a valid readiness signal for serving `initialize`.** It is a
  FastMCP `custom_route` registered deliberately outside the auth middleware and outside the
  DNS-rebinding transport-security guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:210-224`), so it exercises
  none of the auth middleware, the transport-security host/origin guard, the StreamableHTTP
  session manager, or the MCP handshake. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:794-798` gates the nginx
  cutover on that 200 alone and never issues a single `/mcp` request in the whole deploy path.
  Container logs show a container promoted to live traffic 0.9 s after `/health` first answered
  which then did not serve its first `/mcp` request until 54 s later.

## The defect to fix

The readiness contract. This is the same class the project has already ruled on: `store_status`'s
docstring (`_mcp_health.py:118-129`) and its pinning test
(`tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py`) record that `/health` used to report only
`in_flight`, so a container with no ticket store at all passed both the container HEALTHCHECK and
the blue-green readiness gate, and a deployed server answered every tracker query as though the
store were empty for weeks (bugs `kilted-nuclear-bronco` / `mobile-groovy-badger`). The
established invariant is that `/health` must carry enough signal for the blue-green readiness gate
to be meaningful. The MCP request path -- the only thing the container exists to serve -- is still
unrepresented in it. A container whose `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` is wrong answers `/health`
200 while returning 421 to every real request, and the deploy promotes it and logs
"mcp redeployed + healthy".

## Fix

Make the server prove its own MCP request path before it can report ready, and report the result
on `/health`. All of it lands in `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, the module that already owns
`/health`, the in-flight gauge, and the boot store sweep.

1. `run_startup_handshake(mcp, *, budget_seconds)` drives ONE real `initialize` JSON-RPC request
   through the server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` with a synthetic ASGI scope, using a
   `Host` header drawn from the server's configured transport-security allowlist. It exercises the
   transport-security guard, the session manager, and the MCP handshake in-process. It returns
   `{"ok", "status", "elapsed_ms", "budget_ms", "error"}` and NEVER raises -- a health/readiness
   concern that can fail the boot is worse than one that reports a degraded field, exactly as
   `store_status` already argues.
2. The drive is bounded: the ASGI `receive` yields the body once and then `http.disconnect`
   (without which the SSE response stream never terminates -- verified), and the whole drive runs
   under a `budget_seconds` timeout. A timeout is reported as `ok: False`, never as a hang.
3. `wrap_lifespan_with_handshake(app, mcp, ...)` wraps the Starlette app's
   `router.lifespan_context` so the handshake runs AFTER `session_manager.run()` is entered and
   BEFORE uvicorn reports application startup complete. Because uvicorn completes lifespan startup
   before it accepts connections, `/health` answering 200 then proves, by construction, that this
   container has already served a real MCP handshake. `run_http_with_grace` wires it.
4. `/health` gains a `handshake` field beside `in_flight` and `store`, so the signal is
   inspectable by an operator and available to the readiness gate in exactly the shape the `store`
   field already established. The status code stays 200 for the same reason `store` does.

Deliberately NOT in scope: no change to `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`,
`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`, or the clarity/quality gate code. No attempt to shorten the 5.5 s
import cost -- that is a separate, larger piece of work and this change makes it harmless rather
than faster.

## Portability

No CI provider is involved. The handshake runs in-process at container start on any host, in any
environment, with or without a deployment pipeline; the `/health` field is readable by any probe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The dominant contributor to first-`initialize` latency is identified BY MEASUREMENT, and the
      store-size / boto3 / auth / provisioning hypotheses are each explicitly confirmed or refuted
      with numbers. (Recorded in the RCA comment.)
- [ ] `run_startup_handshake` drives a real `initialize` through the server's own session manager
      and returns `ok: True` with an `elapsed_ms` for a correctly configured server.
- [ ] A server whose transport-security host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports
      `ok: False` with the refusing status (421), rather than reporting ready.
- [ ] The handshake never raises and never hangs: a drive that exceeds `budget_seconds` is
      reported as `ok: False` with an error, and boot continues.
- [ ] `/health` reports the handshake result alongside `in_flight` and `store`, and still returns
      200.
- [ ] The handshake runs inside the ASGI lifespan, so it completes before uvicorn accepts its
      first connection.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] RED-first regression test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_startup_handshake.py`, mutation-checked:
      reverting the fix turns it red.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, and
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` all pass.
- [ ] Change pushed to Gerrit for review.

## Interim mitigation already applied

`~/.codex/config.toml` sets `startup_timeout_sec = 120`. That is a client-side tolerance and is not
what closes this.
